title: Surge window leasing and soft-preempt policy for temporary capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a 'surge window leasing' primitive and a coordinated soft-preempt policy for Redwood Dedicated. Objective: let tenants request short-lived reserved capacity windows (minutes->hours) with clear operator controls and predictable amortized billing while enabling graceful degradation and fallbacks when the cluster needs to reclaim capacity. This ticket covers the API surface, autoscaler integration, operator console tooling, billing amortization rules, runtime reclamation behavior (soft-preempt), and metrics/alerts to ensure we meet latency SLOs during reclaim events.
background: Customers run unpredictable LLM workloads and occasionally need short bursts of headroom beyond their committed capacity. Current surge handling has operator-side ad-hoc fixes and produces opaque overage invoices and sudden request drops. We need a first-class lease concept that is timeboxed, revocable with graceful signals, and paired with transparent prorated billing and customer notifications. The autoscaling layer must honor active leases and the runtime should allow for soft reclamation (throttle new sessions, finish in-flight tokens where possible, and route to fallbacks).
design_decisions: 1) Lease granularity: windows expressed in minutes with a minimum of 15 minutes and maximum 8 hours. 2) Billing: amortize cost across requested window and apply prorated overage on partial use; provide optional 'grace credit' to absorb short reclaim events. 3) Reclaim mechanism: soft-preempt that first toggles request acceptance policy (reject new long-running sessions, enable weight-based routing to fallback models), then signals KV-cache eviction candidates, and finally terminates lowest-priority worker lanes if still required. 4) Operator controls: ability to force-reclaim, extend a lease, or convert a lease to committed capacity. 5) Telemetry: record lease lifecycle events and a lease_reclaim_reason tag for downstream billing and incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: - API: tenants can create a surge_lease via API/console specifying duration and peak qps; create/update/delete endpoints covered by integration tests. - Billing: billing service computes prorated invoice line for leases; test vectors for full/partial/unused windows. - Autoscaler: respects active leases and reserves nodes for leased windows; scales down only after lease expiry or operator reclaim. - Runtime: soft-preempt sequence implemented with documented order-of-operations and no surprising 5xx spikes in staging load tests. - Operator UX: console shows active leases with countdown, owner, and reclaim/extend buttons; audit log entries are generated. - Metrics: lease_count, lease_active_qps, lease_reclaims, lease_prorated_charge emitted to metrics pipeline and surfaced in cost dashboards.
tasks: API design: open API spec + OpenAPI docs for /surge_leases (POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE)
Billing: extend billing microservice to accept lease events and compute prorated lines; add unit/integration tests
Autoscaler: lease-aware reservation logic; prevent preemption inside active lease window
Runtime: implement soft-preempt orchestration (throttle new requests -> route fallbacks -> cache eviction -> worker termination)
Operator Console: UI for creating/extending/reclaiming leases; countdown and audit trail
Metrics/Logging: emit lease lifecycle events, add Grafana panels and alert when lease_reclaims > threshold
E2E tests: staging load tests simulating simultaneous leases and resource contention
Docs: runbook for SRE and KB article for customers explaining billing & reclaim behavior
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: sudden reclaim can coroutine-break long token streams -> mitigation: implement soft-preempt in two phases with explicit client-facing 429/upgrade hints and graceful termination window. - Risk: billing confusion -> mitigation: include clear invoice line item names, sample scenarios in docs, and customer notification email template. - Risk: autoscaler complexity -> mitigation: keep initial lease model conservative (min 15m, integer node reservations) and iterate after telemetry shows safety.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind org opt-in; 2) Pilot with 3 internal customers and Redwood test tenants; 3) Monitor metrics for 2 weeks (latency, reclaims, billing deltas); 4) Gradual enablement for all Dedicated customers with opt-in migration path.
monitoring_playbook: - Dashboards: show lease_active_count, lease_reclaim_rate, average_response_time for leased vs non-leased routes. - Alerts: lease_reclaim_rate > 5% over 15m and p50 latency increase > 20% triggers paging SRE. - Postmortem: attach lease_id and reclaim_reason to traces and invoices for root-cause analysis.
